newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Communists accuse army of Colombian massacre plot.
newsitem.headline: Communists accuse army of Colombian massacre plot.

text.p: Communist Party leaders accused the Colombian army on Wednesday of conspiring with right-wing death squads in the massacre of 30 people in a remote village.
The leaders said Communist Party members were among those known to have been killed and others who were still missing after the brutal attack at the weekend on Mapiripan, in eastern Meta province.

Army chief Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett said earlier this week the killings may have been the result of leftist guerrillas clashing with drug traffickers in a region where plantations of coca leaf, the raw material for cocaine, are widespread.
But the Communist Party said the general was covering for anti-Communist death squads financed by landowners.
"Why did Bonett try to cover up for the criminals ... even though it was clear the attack was carried out by paramilitaries?" the Communist Party national executive said.
"These declarations confirm the conspiracy between the army and paramilitary gangs," it added in a statement.

The National Police on Tuesday said the massacre was carried out by 150 members of the so-called Guaviare Front, a new organisation that is part of a nationwide alliance of paramilitary groups called United Self-Defence of Colombia.

Only five corpses have been recovered since the massacre. Red Cross officials believe most of the bodies may never be found because many were dumped in a nearby river or scattered in the surrounding countryside, according to witness accounts.

In a communique issued prior to the massacre, the Guaviare Front said it was financed by "landowners who have decided to defend their lives, peace and property." It pledged to "pacify" the region by "executing" guerrillas and rooting out rebel sympathisers "camouflaged" amid the civilian population.
Army officers frequently accuse the Communist Party of being the political wing of the country's largest guerrilla force, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
